overview.heading: 3 Days Krabi: The Four Islands by Longtail Boat
body: This is the most straightforward Krabi package we offer, and for a lot of travellers it is the right one. Two nights in Ao Nang, one full day on the water covering the four islands that define Krabi's coastline, and no other fixed commitments.

The four-island route runs from Ao Nang beach out into the Andaman Sea by traditional longtail boat or speedboat. Phranang Cave sits at the foot of the Railay headland and holds a shrine to a princess spirit respected by local people. Chicken Island is named for the limestone formation that resembles a chicken's head and neck, and the snorkelling around it is the day's best. Tup Island has a white-sand bar that emerges at low tide, and Poda Island closes the day with a wide beach and clear, shallow water.

The boat returns to your hotel by around 2pm, which leaves the rest of the day open. Krabi rewards that — Ao Nang's beachfront, the night market in Krabi town, or simply the pace of a place that is a good deal quieter than Phuket.

highlights.heading: Why This 3 Days Krabi Package Stands Apart

items.title: The Four Islands by Traditional Longtail
items.body: The route covers Phranang Cave, Chicken Island, Tup Island and Poda Island in a single day from Ao Nang, travelling by traditional longtail boat or speedboat depending on the day and the group. It is the classic Krabi excursion and the reason most people come, taking in shrine caves, snorkelling water, a tidal sandbar and a white-sand beach in one loop of the Andaman Sea.
items.imageAlt: Traditional longtail boat on turquoise water off Krabi

items.title: Chicken Island & the Snorkelling Stop
items.body: Koh Kai takes its name from the limestone formation at its tip, which from the right angle resembles the head and neck of a chicken. The water around it is the day's main snorkelling stop, shallow and clear enough to see reef fish without diving, and the boat anchors long enough to get properly in the water rather than just look at it.
items.imageAlt: Snorkelling in clear shallow water beside a limestone island

items.title: The Tup Island Sandbar
items.body: At low tide a strip of white sand emerges from the sea between Tup Island and its neighbours, and you can walk out along it with water on both sides. It is a genuinely unusual thing to stand on, and it is the photograph most people take home from Krabi. Whether it appears depends on the tide on the day, which is why the boat timings are set around it.
items.imageAlt: White sandbar emerging between islands at low tide, Krabi

items.title: Phranang Cave & Poda Island
items.body: Phranang Cave sits beneath the Railay headland and is well known for the local legends attached to it and for the shrine to a princess spirit that fishermen still honour. Poda Island closes the day: a wide white beach backed by a single limestone outcrop, with shallow, clear water for swimming before the boat turns for Ao Nang.
items.imageAlt: White sand beach and limestone outcrop at Poda Island, Krabi

days.title: Arrive Krabi — Free to Explore
days.description: Met at Krabi International Airport by our local representative and transferred privately to your hotel in Ao Nang. The rest of the day is free. Ao Nang's beachfront strip, its restaurants and the walkway to Nopparat Thara beach are all within easy reach, and the Krabi town night market is a short ride away. Overnight in Krabi.

days.title: Krabi 4 Islands Escapade
days.description: 08:00 hotel pickup and transfer to the pier. 08:30 board a traditional longtail boat or speedboat for the Andaman Sea. Visit Phranang Cave, known for its local legends and the shrine to a princess spirit respected by local people. Snorkel at Chicken Island, named for the limestone formation resembling a chicken's head and neck. Picnic-box lunch is provided. Walk the Tup Island sandbar — the white-sand pathway that appears at low tide — then continue to Poda Island for swimming and snorkelling off its white-sand beach. 14:00 return to your hotel.

sections.heading: 3 Day Krabi Package from Malaysia — The Four Islands
sections.body:
A three-day Krabi package from Malaysia is the shortest trip that still gives you a complete day on the water. Krabi International Airport takes direct traffic from Kuala Lumpur, and Ao Nang — where the boats leave from — is around a 40-minute drive from the terminal.

The four-island tour is the anchor. It leaves the pier at 08:30 and is back at your hotel by around 2pm, which is early enough that the day does not feel spent. The arrival evening and departure morning are left free, which suits Krabi: it is a quieter, more scenic place than Phuket and it rewards not scheduling every hour.

sections.heading: Longtail Boat or Speedboat — Does It Matter?
sections.body:
The four-island route runs on both, and which you travel on depends on the day and the group size. The traditional longtail is slower and noisier, sits low in the water and is the more atmospheric way to see the karsts; the speedboat is faster and drier, and gives you a little more time at each stop.

Neither changes the itinerary — Phranang Cave, Chicken Island, Tup Island and Poda Island are covered either way. If you have a strong preference, tell us when you book and we will match you to an operator running that boat on your dates.

faq.heading: Questions About This 3 Days Krabi Package

items.question: Do Malaysians need a visa for Thailand?
items.answer: No. Malaysian passport holders enter Thailand visa-free for tourism under ASEAN reciprocal arrangements. Requirements and permitted stay can change, so confirm the current position with us or with Thai immigration before you travel.

items.question: Are national park fees included?
items.answer: No. Krabi's national park admission fees — roughly RM50 — are paid on the day and are not included in the package price. Compulsory tour tips of RM39 per person are also excluded.

items.question: Will the Tup Island sandbar be visible?
items.answer: The sandbar appears at low tide, so it depends on the tide on your tour date. Operators plan the route around the tide table where they can, but it is a natural feature rather than a guaranteed one.

items.question: Is Krabi better than Phuket for a quiet trip?
items.answer: Generally yes. Krabi is less developed than Phuket, with dramatic limestone scenery, quieter beaches and a slower pace, which suits travellers who want nature and relaxation over nightlife and shopping. Phuket has the wider choice of restaurants, resorts and evening entertainment.

items.question: Can this be combined with Phuket?
items.answer: Yes. Phuket and Krabi are a few hours apart by road or a shorter hop by sea, and combining them is a popular way to get both the developed island and the quiet one in a single trip. Our Phuket and Krabi guide covers how to structure a combined itinerary.
